plot: You swallow a piece of gum. Gus panics because acid can't dissolve gum base, Cortez hunts for proof of the seven-year rumor and finds none, Liv gets a partly absorbed sweetener box, the housekeeper wave sweeps Chewy Lou through the pyloric door, and Neff times the trip at a couple of days. Tease: a swallowed ice cube.

script.title: Swallowed Gum Stays 7 Years? Your Organs Disagree

episode.action: swallow a piece of chewing gum

beats.title: Swallowed Gum Stays 7 Years? Your Organs Disagree

beats.say: Hold everything! Something rubbery just fell in the pool. It's not food and it's still sweet!
Easy, chef. Name's Chewy Lou. I'm gum. Don't worry, I've got plenty of stretch.
beats.label: Gum base: synthetic rubbers and resins

beats.say: Plenty of stretch? I can't break you down. My acid is pH one point five!
Great. I'll be in the corner. Chewing. Without a mouth. Weird, right?
All hands, emergency meeting! Mouth sent us a package and the label says gum.
Line two is Gus. Line three is Gus. Line four is also Gus. He is yelling!
Quick audit. No calories, no nutrients, no paperwork. Why is it even here?
Because somebody swallowed it. Rumor says it stays for SEVEN YEARS!
Seven years?! Do we have to give it a desk? A badge? A parking spot?
Everyone calm. We check the facts before we panic. Beat, you're on hold music.
Fine, the facts. Door's open. Welcome to my acid bath, Lou.
My acid melts a turkey leg in a few hours. Watch it work!
beats.label: Gastric acid: pH 1.5 to 3.5

beats.say: Ooh, warm. Nice spa. Is this the free sample?
The sweetener is dissolving! The mint flavor is leaving! You're shrinking!
Most of that was gone after the first ten minutes of chewing. Old news.
Okay, but the gum base? The rubbery part? Why won't you break?
Enzymes cut food into small pieces. Nobody gave them a recipe for rubber.
So I can't digest you and I can't dissolve you. This is the worst shift ever!
Fix number one: more acid! Everybody turn the dial up!
Still here. Still stretchy. Do you have a towel? I'm getting a tan.
Fix number two: squash him! Wall muscles, churn like a washing machine!
Fun! I'm a snack-sized stress ball. Do it again, I'm getting smaller sweet parts!
Churning breaks food into mush. You just get squished and bounce back!
Welcome to my gym. Rubber doesn't quit. Rubber doesn't take lunch breaks either.
Evidence time. Neff, pull the files on the seven-year rule.
Searching... searching... Nothing. No study, no lab, no records at all.
The rumor has no source. It's just a thing people tell little cousins.
So nobody ever checked? Then I'm filing this myth under NOPE.
So how long does it really stay? Asking for the front desk.
Gut crews move stuff along all day. Gus, how fast is the road?
The stomach churns, but gum base rides along. The real exit plan is next.
Delivery for the liver! Tiny box of sweetener, still warm from the mouth.
Real sugar I know. This is a sugar alcohol. Gets absorbed only partly.
beats.label: Sorbitol: only partly absorbed by the gut

beats.say: Nothing to filter. Nothing to fix. Honestly, a very short shift.
Lou, I checked your badge. Your rubber part never even reached my door.
Right, I'm not in the blood. I'm just a passenger. Hi, Liv, nice hard hat!
Stop chatting. You're still sitting in my break room and my coffee is cold!
I need to talk to the cleaning crew. Hit the big red button.
Between meals, the stomach sends strong waves down the tube. Little pieces move on.
They call it the migrating motor complex. I call it the housekeeper wave.
beats.label: Migrating motor complex: stomach's cleanup wave

beats.say: Whoa! The floor is moving! It's like a conveyor belt for people with no feet!
It sweeps out stuff I can't digest. Tough pieces, seeds, and you, you rubber ball!
Does it hurt? It looks like it should hurt.
Nope. Just a big hug from the walls. Look, the door!
The stomach's exit is a muscle ring. It opens a little at a time.
Pyloric sphincter, you're up! Open wide for Lou!
beats.label: Pyloric sphincter: the stomach's exit door

beats.say: It's tight in there. I'm a big gum, I've got squishy shoulders.
Everyone out! Squeeze the gum! Left shoulder! Now the right!
I'm through! I'm through! Tell my mom I'm in the small intestine!
Phew! That's a record. A full break room for the first time all day.
Past the exit door is a very long road. The gut keeps squeezing, section after section.
Status? How long will Lou be on the road?
Small intestine takes hours. Then the large intestine adds a day or two.
beats.label: Peristalsis: muscle waves that push food along

beats.say: So he's out in a few days? Not seven years?
Total trip is usually a couple of days. Not years. Not even a week.
Make it official. Beat, write the memo in big letters.
Done. I also ordered a farewell cake. It's mostly air.
One more rule, people. Chew your food, not your rumors.
Noted. Filing that under things the brain says when it wants to look wise.
Ooh, new voicemail. It's Lou from the large intestine. Everything's fine, he says.
Tell him no more questions. Gum is a team player, even when nobody asked.
Day three, folks. Lou here, reporting from the last mile. It got a bit... dark.
Any last words, Lou? Any regrets?
Yes. Spit me out in a napkin next time. The mouth never got a vote.
One piece of gum is a routine passenger for us. Tell the other gums, we've seen it all.
Gotcha. Goodbye, break room. You were warm, loud, and a little acidic.
Case closed. Every myth gets the same treatment: check the facts first.
Next time: someone swallows a whole ice cube and the break room goes frozen.

fact.title: REAL BODY NOTE
lines: It usually exits in a few days.
fact.source: OpenStax A&P 2e; NIDDK Your Digestive System

long.title: Swallowed Gum Stays 7 Years? Your Organs Disagree
long.description:
You swallowed one piece of gum and your organs lost it. Gus can't dissolve Chewy Lou, Cortez tries to file a seven-year rule, and the housekeeper wave finally shows the real road out.
A funny, body-accurate trip through the stomach: acid, the pyloric door, sugar alcohol, and why gum is not stuck for years.
